plain.text: Paul commends Phoebe, a servant (deacon) of the church in Cenchreae, who has helped many, including him. He sends greetings to many friends in Rome: Priscilla and Aquila, his co-workers who risked their lives for him; the church that meets in their house; Andronicus and Junia, outstanding among the apostles; and many others, men and women, who have worked hard in the Lord. "Greet one another with a holy kiss."

Paul urges them to watch out for those who cause divisions and put obstacles in the way of the teaching they learned. Such people serve their own appetites and deceive the naive with smooth talk. He wants them to be wise about what is good and innocent about what is evil. "The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus be with you."

Timothy, Paul's co-worker, and others send greetings. Tertius, who wrote down the letter, greets them too, as does Gaius, Paul's host. (Verse 24 is not found in the earliest manuscripts.) Paul ends with praise to God, who is able to strengthen them by the good news about Jesus Christ, revealing a mystery hidden for long ages but now made known to all nations so they might believe and obey. "To the only wise God be glory forever through Jesus Christ! Amen."

summary.bigIdea: Paul ends with warm greetings to many co-workers, a warning about division, and praise to God.
points: Paul honours many men and women who served alongside him, including Phoebe, Priscilla and Junia.
He warns against people who cause division.
He closes with praise to the only wise God through Jesus Christ.
summary.reflection: Paul named and thanked many people. Who could you thank for their part in your life or faith?
